title: FrontendConformanceCorpus
description: The single machine-readable corpus of authoring-frontend conformance vectors. Each vector states one authored program once — its declarations, its body in a language-neutral statement vocabulary, and what the resulting FrontendGraph, canonical AIR, or compiled artifact must say — and `apxm codegen frontend-conformance` projects it into a runnable harness for every registered authoring language. No language restates a fixture, so a vector added here is a case added to every language at once and a language that does not implement it fails with FrontendConformanceFailure{language, vector, diff}. This corpus carries fixture text and expected facts only; it carries no lowering identity of its own.

type_refs.description: The typed interface declarations every fixture states its Agent interfaces with. Each language projects them into whatever it needs a named type to be.

contexts.description: The Context declarations the corpus shares across vectors. A Context is declared once so both languages give it the same type reference, which is what makes context_type_ref comparable across the two.

ScalarKind.description: The closed set of Context field types each language projects into its own scalar spelling.

MarkerKind.description: The declaration markers a fixture may state. Every one is a name the frontend-surface manifest publishes.

id.description: The vector's stable identity. It names the generated fixture and appears in every failure this vector raises, in both languages.

covers.description: What this vector proves, stated once for both languages.

programs.description: The programs this fixture authors, in source order. The last one is the subject every expectation is evaluated against; the others exist so the subject can compose them.

expect.description: What the captured subject must say. Present when the corpus states the authoring succeeds.

rejects.description: Present when the corpus states the authoring fails. An empty object states only that it fails, which is what a vector says when the two languages reject it with different wording.

message_contains.description: Text every registered language's rejection must state. It is one shared substring, not one language's whole message.

declaration_rejections.description: A vector about declaring a marker rather than authoring a program: every listed marker must reject every listed reference.

references.description: Each entry is a reference the marker must reject. `@handler_object` is the one reserved entry: it means a package-local handler object, which each language projects into its own spelling of one.

name.description: The binding name both languages declare this marker under. It is corpus-wide unique, because the Python projection authors every fixture in one module scope.

target_ref.description: The exact typed reference the declaration binds. For a Skill it is the skill's own id, which is what that marker takes.

instructions.description: Where a Skill's instructions live. Stated only by a Skill declaration. The `entry` branch carries no path: the one package path a skill_id resolves to is derived, so no fixture restates it and no fixture can disagree with the frontends about it.

text.description: The instruction body, stated only by the `inline` branch.

target.description: The declaration the Hook names. Python states it as text and TypeScript as the declared value; both resolve to the same captured intent.

StatementKind.description: The closed statement vocabulary a fixture body is written in. Every entry has a projection in every registered language; adding one means teaching every language to project it.

ExpressionKind.description: The closed expression vocabulary a fixture body is written in. `unawaited_effect` and `plain_call` exist so a vector can state what must be rejected, not only what must be captured.

Expectation.description: One query into a captured program, and the operators that must hold of what it resolves to. A query is `<source>:<path>`, where source is graph, air, artifact, or the bare `diagnostics`, and a path segment is a field name followed by any of `[]` (flatten one level), `[n]` (index), and `[key=value]` (filter).
